title: hwp-edit-report-v1
description: Machine-readable account of what `hwp edit --report <path>` (and `--dry-run`) did: every op's status, how many IR pieces it touched, and the segment ids it changed as before/after pairs. Content-free — no paragraph text, no replacement strings and no user-supplied patterns (T-07-22).

dry_run.description: true when this report came from --dry-run: every op applied against an in-memory copy of the document through the same preflight, apply loop and staged writer/verifier a real run uses, but no output file was published (D-14). A dry-run report and a real-run report of the same batch differ only in this field.

index.description: This op's position in the --ops batch array (Phase 6 D-01 array order).

op.description: The op kind, spelled the same way edit-ops-v1's own "op" field spells it (Phase 6 D-03).

pieces_touched.description: For apply_form_bindings, the number of selected text replacements plus newly cloned profile tables (the original table is not a clone); the receipt separately reports targets and cloned_profiles, and changed remains empty. For insert_blocks, the number of inserted top-level paragraphs (one per accepted block, equal to blocks.len(); table cell paragraphs are inside their table and not counted). The ids of the inserted segments are in changed. For other operations, how many IR nodes this op actually mutated: the number of canonical runs whose shape id changed for a run-range char-format op, the number of segment ids (paragraph and/or run) an addressed op's own target touched otherwise, and never less than 1 for an applied op that changed the document — an "applied: 1" summary must never hide a multi-piece write (D-02). An applied op whose result was already in effect (a `style_tables` on already-styled tables, or a `set_table_placement` to the placement the table already has) changed nothing and reports 0 (#359).

changed.description: Before/after segment id pairs this op changed (D-13). insert_blocks reports one creation pair (before null) for every segment `hwp cat --segments v2` publishes inside the inserted top-level paragraphs, in document order, in the state right after that op: each paragraph id followed by its run ids and, for a table or image block, the table, cell and image ids. An inserted top-level paragraph with no published segment (an empty or break-only one) is named by its paragraph id, which a fresh `hwp cat --segments v2` does not list but move_para and delete_para accept (#521). A run id is what set_format addresses. pieces_touched counts the inserted paragraphs, not these pairs. Empty for an op with no address (a text-anchor/pattern match, which has no segment id to report) or one that changed nothing identifiable. A run-range char-format op that splits a run reports the touched paragraph's OWN id change AND the id change of every LATER run in that paragraph, not only the run it targeted — splitting a run shifts every later run's canonical index and therefore its id, even though that run's own text and shape are untouched; reporting only the targeted run's pair would leave a consumer re-keying against ids that no longer exist.

missing_style.description: Selected missing-style policy for applied insert_blocks only; omitted for every other outcome. The request defaults to create. This is policy metadata, not a failure reason.

changed_total.description: Present only when this op produced more id pairs than the 10000 that `changed` may carry: the real number of pairs. `changed` then holds the first 10000 in document order and the rest are not listed; they are still addressable, because every id is the one `hwp cat --segments v2` publishes for the output. Absent means `changed` is complete. A valid insert_blocks request can exceed the cap (for example one 100 x 50 table publishes 15002 segments: the paragraph, the table, and a cell, a cell paragraph and a run for each of its 5000 cells), and this field keeps the report valid instead of dropping the edit's id list silently.

reason.description: Populated only when status is "failed"; null when applied. A fixed, content-free label: usually `<op>: <cause>`, naming the op kind and the failure class (for example `replace: no match`, `create_field: anchor not found`), and a fixed notice for an op whose miss preflight already reported (an unresolved `set_cell_by_label` label). It never repeats the request's patterns, replacement strings, anchors, names or urls, nor any document text (#348). Its wording may change between releases; match on `op` and `status`, not on this text.

before.description: The segment id before this op applied. null marks a creation — the segment did not exist before the batch.

after.description: The segment id after this op applied. null marks a removal — the segment no longer exists after the batch.
